_what: Stated BEFORE the ledger gate was ever run. R10: the falsifier for 'X is wired' is an artifact X produced whose content varies with its input — and a prediction is only evidence if it is written down first. Same discipline as the net-benefit flip point (3,836,739.6 ns), which was solved and recorded before the pair was run.

_state_at_prediction.gate: wired into registry.rs::claim_audit, last check in canonical order

predictions.claim: With an empty ledger, a two-input f32 Add on static shapes declines, and its only decline code is `unproven`.
predictions.derivation: domain ai.onnx; op_type Add; row window 7..=OPSET_ANY renders 7+; two f32 inputs and one f32 output render f32,f32>f32; kernel!(EwBinary,"add") stems! prefix ew_binary gives ew_binary_add_f32; all extents literal gives static; Add has no optional-input table entry so the populated set degrades to arity n2.

predictions.claim: The counters JSON from that run reports proven_key_lookups > 0, ledger_hits as the STRING "UNOBSERVABLE" (not 0 — the baked ledger holds no entries, so a hit could not have occurred in this frame), unproven_declines > 0, ledger_gate ALL-DECLINED, unproven_forms_enabled [].

After the generator writes an entry for exactly the P1 key and the artifact is rebuilt, the SAME model claims the node, ledger_hits becomes an INTEGER >= 1, ledger_gate becomes ALL-PROVEN, and unproven_declines returns to 0. The type of ledger_hits changes with the input; an increment can forge a number and cannot forge a type.

Phi-3.5's claimed-node count goes 355 -> 0 with the gate armed and an empty ledger. Every node declines [unproven] or an earlier code; the EP claims nothing and the model runs entirely on CPU, correctly.

An f16 Add and an f32 Add of the same graph shape produce two DIFFERENT keys, differing only in the dtype component. This is the arms_must_differ control: a probe whose two arms report the same key is a perfectly stable, perfectly wrong answer.

A planted proof key that is in the ledger for f32 does NOT satisfy an f16 node of the same op — the lookup misses and the f16 node declines [unproven] — which is the 2026-07-30 defect made unrepresentable rather than discouraged.

P7_planted_control.rationale: ledger has Mul f32 but not Mul f16; dtype is a path difference so the keys differ
